Policy (Brazilian Portuguese, same as Italian): proper names and names invented by GW2 stay in English (people, places, factions, skills, traits, boons, conditions, stats and their combinations); common objects and concepts are translated, one name for each thing. Base glossary: weapons, rarities, bags, siege, crafting disciplines, stat and duration lines; everything else still in English, to be extended. patterns = whole-line rules, {X} = the prefix words or a number.

advice.ascended: The adjective "ascended" (an item rarity) is "ascendido", agreeing in gender and number with its noun: "ascended armor" = "armadura ascendida", "ascended weapons" = "armas ascendidas", "ascended rings" = "anéis ascendidos".
advice.Focus: "Focus" as an item is the off-hand weapon: "Foco" (plural "Focos"), "focus skills" = "habilidades do Foco". As a verb ("focus on") translate it normally ("concentre-se").
advice.staff: "Staff" as a weapon is "cajado" ("o cajado", plural "cajados"). When "staff" means the people who work somewhere, translate it as "equipe".
advice.glider: "Glider" (the equipment used for gliding) is "planador", plural "planadores".
advice.skin: "Skin" of an item (weapon, armor, back item, glider, mount, wardrobe) stays "skin" in Portuguese: a feminine loanword ("a skin", "as skins"). In item names the skin comes first, then the object named in the English name, with the article: "Iron Axe Skin" = "Skin do Machado de ferro". Translate only the object that the English name contains, never add a weapon or an armor piece that is not there: when the name has no object word, write "Skin de" and the name. "weapon skins" = "skins de armas", "armor skins" = "skins de armaduras", "This will unlock the skin in your wardrobe" = "Isto desbloqueia a skin no seu guarda-roupa". Never "pele", "aparência" or "visual" for a cosmetic skin. Only when it is the skin of a body (a person, an animal, a creature) translate "skin" as "pele".
advice.meet: "Meet" in quest objectives and with characters the player already knows means going to someone or joining them: "Encontre", "Encontre-se com", "Reúna-se com" ("Meet Logan at his office." = "Encontre o Logan no escritório dele.", "Meet with your allies" = "Reúna-se com seus aliados", "Meet me at the temple." = "Encontre-me no templo."). "Meet with" and "meet up" are never "conhecer". Use "conhecer" only when people meet for the first time: "Nice to meet you" = "É um prazer conhecê-lo", "How did you two meet?" = "Como vocês se conheceram?", "Meet the locals" = "Conheça os habitantes locais".
advice.met: "Met" (past of "meet") usually means the player went to find or joined someone already known: "I met Gorrik at the gates" = "Encontrei o Gorrik nos portões". Use "conhecer" only for a first meeting: "the day we met" = "o dia em que nos conhecemos".

advice.Icebrood: "Icebrood" is "a Prole do Gelo": a feminine singular collective noun. Always use feminine singular articles and agreement: "a Prole do Gelo", "da Prole do Gelo", "contra a Prole do Gelo", never "os Prole". In names "Icebrood X" becomes "X da Prole do Gelo". The story name "The Icebrood Saga" stays in English.
advice.forged: "Forged" with a capital letter, as a noun or before a name, refers to the Forged, Balthazar's army: "os Forjados" (one member = "um Forjado"); before a name use "dos Forjados" ("Forged Soldier" = "Soldado dos Forjados"). When "forged" means made at a forge, translate it normally ("forjado").
